library_load_paths.question: Where do the five @deepseek-ai libraries of the imported harness come from, and could the checkout or the cwd win?
library_load_paths.anchor: createRequire(join(nodeModules, 'package.json')) where nodeModules = owningNodeModules(realpath of the measured binary); never the checkout, never cwd.
library_load_paths.fallback_note: The fallback is the measured install's ancestors and node's global folders — not the checkout, not the cwd. If a library were absent from the measured install, node would keep looking, so the file's own first measured row ("every library these tests import comes from the install that was measured") is the guard that such a fallback cannot pass unnoticed. That row is not vacuous: the commit's unit test puts a decoy copy in a checkout node_modules and a second copy in the measured install and shows the measured one wins.
library_load_paths.wrong_version_override_is_not_answered: A refused binary resolution is returned verbatim by resolveDshLibraries (same reason string, same searched list, nodeModules/require null), so an explicit wrong-version override cannot reach an implicit install through the import path.

unverified: The commit message's per-file evidence does not match the tree: it says "29 tests pass (dsh-entry 17, tool-discovery 4, smoke 8)". At 455cd4ca the same three files give dsh-entry 19, tool-discovery 8, smoke 2 — total 29, so the total reproduces while the breakdown does not. The files are right and the total is right; the sentence is wrong and should not be quoted as evidence.

The guard that keeps a refusal from becoming a skip (the resolveDshLibraries rows in dsh-entry.test.mjs) is outside `npm test`: npm test lists nine files and dsh-entry.test.mjs, runtime.terminal-plan.test.mjs and runtime.finished-plan.test.mjs are not among them. That is pre-existing (package.json untouched by either attempt), and tool-discovery.test.mjs still catches the coarser mutant M1 loudly, but under M2 `npm test` with a bad override would be green with one skip. I did not find another in-`npm test` file that would redden for M2.

If a library were missing from the measured install but present in one of the fallback directories (install ancestors, /node_modules, node's global folder), node would load that one; only the file's own attribution row would redden. I did not build that case because it would require writing node_modules above the shared host install, which is out of my scope. Reasoning is static plus the commit's own decoy-copy unit test.
Non-symlink .bin installs (Windows), MAX_WALK depth beyond 8 directories, and installs nested inside another package's node_modules were not exercised.
Only the pinned node v24.22.2 was used. The brief says /usr/bin/node v22 gives different results, so nothing here speaks for v22.

The six runtime e2e files were exercised against their own local fixture servers (I checked each child env sets AITELIER_URL to a local server) and not against a live AItelier service; no production service was touched.
No pytest was run (node-only review, per the brief).
